transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Orion Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Orion Platform Eng), Tom Reynolds (Orion Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed week-over-week POC metrics; pinned two candidate models for canary testing (redwood-v2-small-q4 and redwood-v2-medium-fp16).
- Discussed rollback/fallback strategy and latency vs cost tradeoffs; agreed to run additional 50k-token benchmark and to validate KV cache hit rates.
- Action items: share pinned config, run benchmarks, provide sample data, schedule canary planning.

Topics:
- Model selection rationale
- Version pinning and rollbacks
- Benchmark results discrepancies (tail latency spikes)
- Security/ops: VPC routing, audit logs, SSO needs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: okay great good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick sync on the poc progress and focus on model selection and pinning. priya is on to run through the bench results.
[00:12] Priya: hey all, yeah i pulled the end-to-end numbers, um i have cost and latency split by route and by config, couple of notes first — the small quantized model (redwood-v2-small-q4) is about 2.4x cheaper per token than the fp16 medium, median latency is ~110ms vs 85ms for medium but tail spikes are higher on small when KV cache miss happens.
[00:35] Carlos: when you say tail spikes like how high are we talking? our SLA target is 200ms p99 for UI calls.
[00:43] Priya: p99 for small hit ~420ms in the synthetic tests, for medium fp16 it was ~185ms. interestingly the caching profile on your sample workload is pretty bursty so kv cache miss rate was ~18% which magnifies the small model's spikes.
[01:05] Aisha: yeah we saw similar — our traffic has those long doc retrievals that blow the sequence length. question: is the q4 quantization causing the spikes or is it just compute saturation?
[01:17] Priya: good question, preliminary look says it's compute + attention kernel behavior under longer sequences; quantization does add a little bit of CPU overhead on the host but not the dominant factor. we'll run a dedicated test with longer sequences pinned to see.
[01:33] Tom: also curious about fallback: if we pin the smaller model for cost but it violates the p99 occasionally, can we do automatic fallback to medium? what's the latency penalty for fallback?
[01:43] Jordan: yes that's exactly the pattern we recommend — configured routing: try small, if p99 or token timeout exceed threshold, failover to medium. fallback adds about 20–40ms as we re-route and warm kv cache, but overall reduces cost on average.
[01:58] Carlos: can we do canary on a subset of traffic? we want to see real behavior not just synth tests.
[02:04] Jordan: absolutely, canary by user segment or by route; typical approach is 5–10% of production traffic with monitoring and automatic rollback.
[02:12] Priya: quick note — in your current dedicated pool the memory/seq capacity seems to be slightly under-provisioned for the medium model at your target concurrency; we can recommend either burst capacity or a slightly bigger instance shape. that will reduce p99.
[02:26] Aisha: do you have recommended instance types? we're running a mix of gpus via our infra teams.
[02:31] Priya: for medium fp16, on average we recommend A40/80-like profile or p4d-ish depending on throughput. for the q4 small cluster the util is lower so cheaper VMs suffice. i'll include a config suggestion in the pinned config.
[02:45] Carlos: security question — are the audit logs preserved for fallback events? we need forensic traces for any model switch.
[02:51] Jordan: yes, we log routing decisions, model versions, input hashes and response meta in the audit trail; can be exported to your SIEM. we'll include a sample log extract.
[03:02] Tom: another operational question — how do we pin versions in the console? is it per-route?
[03:08] Priya: yes per-route and you can pin a list with fallbacks and weights. the UI and API both let you set ordered fallbacks, plus canary percentage. we can export the JSON config too so you can check it into infra repo.
[03:20] Carlos: priya, you mentioned kv cache hit rate was 82% — any immediate tuning we can do?
[03:26] Priya: two levers: prefix caching (increase TTL for repeated prompts) and shaping requests (truncate non-essential context). also more aggressive batching helps throughput without harming p99 if you keep latency SLOs in policy. we'll propose TTL and batching params.
[03:40] Aisha: ok thanks. request: we want the pinned config and the fallback policy as an artifact so our infra can review.
[03:47] Jordan: noted — i'll share pinned-config.json and a short README on rollout steps.
[03:52] [04:00] Priya: quick caveat — the quantized small model had a couple of hallucination cases on long instruction windows in week 2. not huge but visible. medium fp16 was cleaner. if output quality is top priority medium is safer.
[04:15] Carlos: hmm that's concerning. how many cases and can we reproduce?
[04:20] Priya: on the evaluation harness we flagged ~7 out of 1k prompts that deviated vs baseline; i'll include the exact prompts and model outputs.
[04:28] Tom: can we do a staged pin: start with small for low-risk routes (search summarization) and medium for high-risk routes (checkout assistant)?
[04:35] Jordan: yes that's the recommended approach, route-level granularity. also you can set weighted traffic split if you want a soft roll.
[04:42] Carlos: timeline — we want canary next week if benchmarks look good. is that feasible?
[04:47] Priya: we can have benchmarks and pinned configs by Friday; can run canary planning on Thursday.
[04:52] Aisha: deps from our side: need to share masked sample data and confirm canary users. we'll prioritize that.
[04:58] Jordan: great. last bit — pricing impact: if you pin small with fallback to medium on 10% of traffic, we estimate ~35% cost savings vs always medium. detailed numbers will be in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Carlos: please share the spreadsheet.
[05:16] Jordan: will do. ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and action items?
[05:24] Tom: quick note, any constraints around SSO/SAML for the console? we're using okta.
[05:28] Jordan: yes Redwood supports SAML/Okta SSO and RBAC; we'll include SSO onboarding doc.
[05:34] Priya: action recap: i'll run the 50k-token bench, include kv cache tuning suggestions, and push pinned-config.json draft.
[05:42] Aisha: i'll upload sample data and a short doc with traffic profiles.
[05:46] Carlos: i'll loop in security for the audit log review.
[05:50] Jordan: perfect thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the canary planning.

End of recording.
